dedupe_keys.name: dataset bundle for building automation and control systems security analysis knx university of coimbra

description: This bundle holds network captures from the KNX home and building automation system of a real three-floor single-family house, recorded both in normal operation and during several kinds of attack. The house system controls lighting, blinds, radiator heating and the alarm, with light and motion detectors indoors and weather sensors outside, and devices sit on a KNX twisted-pair bus in power and control cabinets on each floor and in an annex. The README describes the house topology room by room and how each dataset can support security analysis of KNX building automation. Coverage: one house in Portugal. Access: free on GitHub under the MIT licence, and on IEEE DataPort as a standard dataset with DOI 10.21227/16a5-m134. Licence: MIT on the GitHub copy. Caveats: a single residential installation, so traffic volumes and device mixes differ from large commercial buildings; the attack set is the authors' own. Simulation uses are intrusion detection training, normal-operation baselines for building control twins and studies of how control-network attacks affect occupants. Related records: the KNXnet/IP intrusion detection dataset from the AI4CYBER project, BACnet packet captures and NREL's cyber-induced mechanical faults dataset.
